opportunities.title: RFP 902737 EVACUATION PLANNING SOFTWARE SOLUTION
opportunities.description: It is the intent of these specifications, terms, and conditions to describe the evacuation planning solution being requested by the Alameda County Sheriff's Office (ACSO) for the Office of Emergency Services (OES). Contractor must provide a secure, cloud-based evacuation planning and modeling software solution capable of supporting evacuation analysis, scenario planning, operational decision-making, and real-time evacuation management. The proposed solution must support Alameda County OES and all Operational Area partners, including fourteen (14) incorporated cities, special districts, County departments, and critical infrastructure partners. The platform must be scalable and configurable to allow jurisdiction-specific access while maintaining Operational Area-level visibility, coordination capability, and governance. The Contractor must provide full implementation services, including configuration, data integration, training, technical support, and ongoing maintenance. The County intends to award a three (3)-year contract (with the option to renew for two [2] years) to the Bidder selected as the most responsive and responsible Bidder whose response conforms to the RFP and meets the County’s requirements.

opportunities.title: GPS Asset Tracking Solution
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena's Department of Public Works provides fleet maintenance services to City vehicles and equipment. The Department is seeking a vendor to provide comprehensive geolocational tracking and telematic hardware and software services for the City's fleet of vehicles and equipment. The selected vendor shall provide all hardware and software related to real-time tracking of the fleet. This should include equipment, storage of telematics data, training, and support. The City has a strong preference for a SaaS/cloud/hosted solution. The target start of the contract term is January 2027 with a term of five (5) years.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: CHIP and CHA implementation, Governance, Community Engagement, and Data Integration Support
opportunities.description: San Mateo County Health, Public Health, Policy & Planning (County) seeks proposals from qualified consulting firms or organizations to provide specialized expertise in a time-limited capacity to provide advisory, facilitation, and capacity-building services supporting the County’s Community Health Improvement Plan (CHIP) and Community Health Assessment (CHA). The selected contractor will provide independent subject-matter expertise, structured facilitation, planning tools, technical consultation, coaching, and implementation-readiness recommendations. The work will help the County establish an effective CHIP/CHA governance structure; refine engagement approaches and implementation protocols; strengthen coordination with trusted-messenger community-based organizations (“CBOs”) and the CHIP backbone organization; and prepare the County to conduct comprehensive, equity-centered CHA/CHIP for future cycles. This procurement is for defined professional consulting deliverables. It is not intended to provide ongoing operational staffing, fill a County position, or delegate the County’s continuing public-health planning, program-management, data-governance, community-engagement, or policy-making responsibilities. The County will retain responsibility for the operational delivery of the CHA, including County decisions; community-engagement fieldwork; participant recruitment; survey administration; incentive administration; identifiable-data stewardship; language access services; final analysis and validation; and preparation, approval, and issuance of the final CHA/CHIP reports. Contract Structure Maximum contract amount: $85,000, not to exceed. Recommended contract term: 9–12 months, beginning after full execution of the County agreement. One contractor award is recommended. Compensation should be deliverable-based; payment is contingent on County review and acceptance of work products in accordance with the deliverable requirements and acceptance process described in this solicitation. No work may begin before the agreement is fully executed and the contractor receives authorization to proceed.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: Access Control System Replacement and Maintenance
opportunities.description: The Department of Public Works is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to replace the County’s existing access control systems with a modern, centralized, and open-architecture solution across more than 40 County locations. The County currently operates the P2000 access control system from Johnson Controls across the majority of its facilities, with one building utilizing a standalone system provided by Open Options. The selected firm for this equipment, services and installation contract will be responsible for the comprehensive delivery of the new system, including planning, procurement, installation, configuration, and integration, and a separate contract will be awarded for ongoing support, in accordance with the project design and specifications.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: Virtual Blood Bourne Pathogens Course
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo (the “County” or “SMC”) covers most of the San Francisco Peninsula. The region covers 744 mi and is home to nearly 800,000 residents and 20 incorporated cities. The County provides for the health and welfare of all people within its borders and serves as the local government for the unincorporated areas. Innovation thrives here in industries including bioscience, computer software, green technology, hospitality, financial management, health care, education and transportation. The County prides itself on how that prosperity fosters its commitment to protecting and enhancing the health, safety, welfare and natural resources of the community. The agency is seeking qualified vendors to provide a virtual Bloodborne Pathogens training course for employees. The goal of this solicitation is to identify an engaging, accessible, and user-friendly online training solution that provides employees with the knowledge and practical guidance necessary to recognize and prevent occupational exposure to bloodborne pathogens and to respond appropriately to potential exposures. The selected vendor should provide a high-quality virtual course that is appropriate for workplace use, supports employee participation and completion, and includes a method for documenting or verifying successful completion. Vendors are encouraged to propose solutions that offer clear instruction, engaging content, convenient online access, and reliable reporting or recordkeeping capabilities.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — City of Pasadena, CA
opportunities.title: Wood Pole Inspection, Treatment, Repair, and UAV Inspection Services
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena Water and Power Department (“PWP”) is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced firms to provide wood pole inspection, repair, restoration, treatment, and related reporting services for PWP’s electric distribution system. The selected firm will support PWP’s ongoing maintenance and compliance program for wood poles, including visual inspections, intrusive inspections, groundline inspections, preservative treatments, minor corrective repairs, pole reinforcement recommendations, installation of approved repair materials, and detailed reporting of observed conditions. PWP’s wood pole program is intended to support safe, reliable, and compliant operation of the electric distribution system in accordance with applicable requirements, including California Public Utilities Commission (“CPUC”) General Order 95, Rules for Overhead Electric Line Construction, and CPUC General Order 165, Inspection Requirements for Electric Distribution and Transmission Facilities. PWP’s system includes approximately 11,000 wood poles, including both municipally owned and jointly owned poles. A significant portion of the pole population is located in rear property or otherwise constrained access locations. The scope of services may include, but is not limited to, pole condition assessment, identification of structural damage or decay, inspection for General Order 95 infractions, groundline and below-ground inspections, preservative and fumigant treatment, installation of visibility strips, guy guards, ground molding, pole tags, and steel truss reinforcement where approved by PWP. The selected firm shall also provide detailed inspection records, photographs, condition ratings, repair recommendations, and electronic data deliverables in a format acceptable to PWP. In addition to conventional field inspection and treatment services, PWP intends to include drone or other unmanned aerial vehicle (“UAV”) inspection services under the resulting contract. UAV services may be used to supplement field inspections, improve access to difficult or hazardous locations, document pole-top conditions, capture high-resolution imagery, and support more efficient assessment of pole attachments, crossarms, hardware, conductors, insulators, and other visible overhead facilities. UAV services shall be performed by qualified, FAA-compliant personnel and in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements. The selected firm shall furnish all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, vehicles, tools, technology, software, transportation, permits, methods, processes, and incidentals necessary to complete the work in accordance with the final scope of services, applicable laws and regulations, industry standards, and PWP requirements.

opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo (“County”) covers most of the San Francisco Peninsula. The region covers 744 mi 2 and is home to approximately 750,000 residents. The County is made up of 20 incorporated cities. The County provides for the health and welfare of all people within its borders and serves as the local government for the unincorporated areas. Innovation thrives here in industries including bioscience, computer software, green technology, hospitality, financial management, health care, education, and transportation. The County prides itself on how that prosperity fosters its commitment to protecting and enhancing the health, safety, welfare, and natural resources of the community. The San Mateo County Parks Department (“Department”) serves nearly three million visitors every year. Visitors have many options when visiting the County’s unique park system. With 24 parks and recreation areas, over 16,000 acres of park land, and 190 miles of trails, the Department provides healthy outdoor activities, educational opportunities, and lasting memories. Due to the diversity of the park system, visitors can enjoy an array of recreational opportunities, including walking; running; hiking; picnicking; horseback riding; kite surfing; fishing; camping; gardening; tide pooling; volunteering; learning; sports courts; and playing on playgrounds.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: Technology of Participation (ToP)
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo (the “County” or “SMC”) covers most of the San Francisco Peninsula. The region covers 744 square miles and is home to nearly 800,000 residents and 20 incorporated cities. The County provides for the health and welfare of all people within its borders and serves as the local government for the unincorporated areas. Innovation thrives here in industries including bioscience, computer software, green technology, hospitality, financial management, health care, education and transportation. The County prides itself on how that prosperity fosters its commitment to protecting and enhancing the health, safety, welfare and natural resources of the community. Formed in July 2014, the San Mateo County Sustainability Department strives to improve the sustainability of the County’s operations and the greater community through work that is designed to bring solutions today while solving for tomorrow. The Sustainability Department has programs to help the county both fight and prepare for climate change, ensure clean energy, water, and air, and conserve resources for future generations through waste reduction. The Sustainability Department has approximately 40 staff members and provides services in the following areas: Communications, Climate Resilience, Climate Protection, Waste Reduction, and Special Districts with similar but varying community needs. The department is seeking a vendor that will provide meeting facilitation using Technology of Participation as a core aspect of the facilitation. We are also looking to have staff trained with these skills and philosophy.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — City of Pasadena, CA
opportunities.title: Power Delivery General Engineering Services
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena is seeking qualified professional engineering firms to supplement its internal resources within the Water and Power Department (PWP), Power Delivery Division. Engineering services provided under the resulting contracts will support the safe, reliable, and efficient operation, maintenance, modernization, and improvement of PWP's electric power delivery system. Engineering services under this RFP are organized into the following Scope of Work Groups: Receiving Station and Substation Design SCADA, Automation, Communications, and Control Design System Planning Civil and Structural Engineering Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Renewable Energy, Energy Storage, Interconnection, and Technical Advisory Services Associated services, including construction management, inspection, drafting, and other technical support, may be required as part of an individual task order where applicable to the assigned Scope of Work Group. Engineering services under the resulting contracts are intended to supplement, not replace, PWP's internal engineering resources. Consultants may be assigned work based on project-specific needs, staff availability, schedule requirements, temporary workload conditions, and the need for specialized expertise. All consultant designs and deliverables shall be subject to review and approval by the responsible PWP engineering group. Consultants shall not supervise City employees or exercise project management authority over City staff. Work that is ongoing, predictable, or programmatic over multi-year periods will generally be performed by permanent PWP staff. The City intends to award multiple contracts under this solicitation to establish a pool of qualified engineering consultants. Work will be authorized through individual task orders based on the requirements of the assignment, including consultant availability, applicable expertise, capacity, schedule, and other considerations identified by the City. Award of a contract does not guarantee any minimum quantity or value of work. Current priority programs anticipated for consultant support include, but are not limited to: SCE Upgrade of the TMG 220 kV Gould Circuit; Jungle-MUX Fiber Optic Upgrades; SCADA/OMS/DMS upgrades; Mobile Substation protection, housing, and station upgrades; substation equipment specifications; EV charging infrastructure at Aquatic Center, Sunset Reservoir, and Del Mar Garage; the Avon Ramp and Arroyo Charging Depots Progressive Design-Build project; Municipal Solar, Energy Storage, and Resilience Projects; System Impact Studies for Large Resource Interconnections; System Modeling for Compliance Studies; TMG Receiving Station capacity studies; and Subtransmission System short-circuit current reduction studies. This list is illustrative and does not constitute a guarantee that any particular project or assignment will be issued under the resulting contracts. Proposers must demonstrate, at a minimum, five (5) years of relevant experience and at least five (5) completed projects within the past five (5) years for each Scope of Work Group proposed. Consultant staff shall include engineers registered in the State of California in the relevant disciplines, including civil, electrical, structural, mechanical, control systems, and/or fire protection engineering, as applicable to the services being performed. Specific minimum qualifications for each Scope of Work Group are stated in Section 6.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — City of Pasadena, CA
opportunities.title: P-57907 Enterprise Monitoring
opportunities.description: The City of Pasadena is seeking a vendor to provide an Enterprise Monitoring solution and associated implementation and support services. The goal of the Enterprise Monitoring project is to strengthen alert management and monitoring processes , and to proactively identify and address system performance issues before they impact customers. The City seeks a unified monitoring and observability platform that provides centralized visibility across infrastructure, networks, cloud services, databases, applications, integrations, and business services. The desired solution will correlate events and performance data across technology domains, improve operational awareness, reduce alert fatigue, accelerate root cause analysis, and enable proactive management of service health and availability. The platform should support the City's current hybrid and multi-cloud environment while providing a scalable foundation for future operational monitoring and automation initiatives.

opportunities.source_name: OpenGov — County of San Mateo, CA
opportunities.title: Domain Transition and Implementation Services RFP
opportunities.description: The County of San Mateo (County) Technology Services Department (TSD) is seeking proposals from qualified contractors to fully transition the County from our current smcgov.org domain name to a .gov domain name in compliance with California Assembly Bill 1637 requiring all local agencies to adopt a .gov domain name for public websites and email addresses no later than January 1, 2029. This technical migration encompasses all County website domains and subdomains, email, Domain Name Systems (DNS), TSD owned and managed enterprise applications connected to Okta and Active Directory for authentication, enterprise platforms, and identifying departmental applications countywide impacted by this domain name transition.
